findings.title: Check complete journal writes before treating custody as durable
findings.trigger: os.write(fd,data) returns a positive count smaller than len(data), for example an ordinary partial write, while fsync succeeds.
findings.finding: event() ignores the returned byte count and still returns success. service() can then publish ACK after a truncated registered/ack-intent journal record. events in memory remain complete, and final real validation checks snapshot plus journal file membership/size but never parses/reconciles the authoritative journal, so it can report clean custody despite violating durable-before-ACK. This is a concrete partial-write case, not an arbitrary OS-stall requirement.
findings.requested_change: Use a full-write loop or checked buffered write with fsync; retain cleanup ownership and close grants on zero/short/unrecoverable write. Validate journal records and sequence/identity against accepted transitions before a clean receipt. Apply checked writes to native raw audit append as needed for complete retained evidence. Add a focused short-write/truncated-journal control that cannot obtain an ACK or pass clean custody.

findings.title: Persist completion acceptance before publishing the leader exit grant
findings.trigger: Root processes a validated completion and publishes exit.json, then fails or is interrupted before event(suffix,...).
findings.finding: The completion SHA/child wait are updated in memory, exit-grant-intent is journaled without completion detail, exit grant is published, and the full completion journal event is written afterwards. This reverses the selected contract journal/acceptance order. The exit grant itself already binds completion_sha256 and the wrapper completion file is durable, so this is narrower than a launch-without-custody flaw.
findings.requested_change: Prefer fsyncing the validated full completion/hash acceptance event before publishing exit grant. Alternatively root must explicitly select the immutable grant file as the durable acceptance record and terminal validation must verify that record/completion binding rather than imply a prior completion journal event. Test failure at the acceptance/exit-grant boundary and do not release based only on in-memory state.

findings.title: Distinguish nine proposed controls from untested signal and I/O fault paths
findings.finding: cancel-after-ack flips a manager cancellation list and never delivers INT/TERM/HUP to wrapper; journal-failure replaces event() with a throw before the actual write; immutable-and-bindings directly checks helpers and sticky state rather than exercising malformed ACK/replay through the wrapper. None of the nine cases injects a short write, asserts durable acceptance/grant order, or drives the wrapper signal-mask/native-wait path. Output-overflow, missing completion and late/partial registration are likewise not runtime controls in this plan.
findings.requested_change: Add narrowly bounded fake-child controls for the journal durability/order fixes and an actual selected wrapper signal during acknowledged native work (or keep that path explicitly pending and prohibit real-runtime acceptance until separately checked). Retain no-ACK zero-launch, cancellation-racing ownership, exact child wait/group absence and scratch-preservation assertions. Do not describe helper-only tests or timeout as evidence for actual signal delivery behavior. No such control is run by this review.

OCR-A3 request/ACK/child/completion/exit binding contains run nonce, phase, ordinal, recipe ID, invocation nonce, wrapper PID/PGID, request and ACK hashes. Real recipes constrain exact ordered argv and private fixture key directories.
